spot.html_text: The first part is closely tied to Dedekind’s employment of set-theoretic tools and techniques. He uses these to construct new mathematical objects (the natural and real numbers, ideals, etc.) or whole classes of such objects (algebraic number fields, rings, modules, lattices, etc.), usually in terms of infinite sets.
